chunks: Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked him about a man who pronounced ẓihār against his wife five times or more, so he said:
ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “In place of every single time, there is an expiation.”

key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: pronounced ẓihār; declared his wife unlawful through the formula of resemblance
key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: an expiation required for the violation

ai.seo_question: If a man pronounces ẓihār against his wife multiple times, is one kaffārah enough or is there a separate expiation for each time?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding repeated ẓihār pronounced against one's wife. It states that each separate occurrence entails its own kaffārah, showing that repeated statements are treated as carrying repeated legal consequence.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4834 - Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Imam (as) about a man who declared ẓihar (a form of divorce by comparison) against his wife five times or more.
Imam (as) replied: "Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:
'For every instance, there is a separate expiation.'"
